title: Explain distinct requirement and design authorship
statement: The Authoring guidance Module shall explain distinct requirement and design authorship within its accountable boundary so that SR-081 can be satisfied without transferring another owner's decisions or state authority.

what.problem: The SR-081 obligation crosses guidance, governance or publication boundaries; an unowned contribution can make a locally valid step appear sufficient for the whole workflow.
what.desired_outcome: Keep IR/SR and stakeholder intent, logical Functions, and Module/Interface/AR realization under their respective authoring methods.

why.rationale: MOD-008 owns the behavior or state needed for this contribution; separating it preserves one accountable owner while allowing the parent SR to compose several contributors.

stakeholders: Authors, reviewers and project decision owners

conditions: When the selected requirement-first workflow exercises SR-081 or reassesses its affected basis.

contexts: The MOD-008 responsibility boundary and its declared logical Interfaces.

how.approach: Apply the allocated criteria through the constrained Functions and explicit contract inputs/outcomes; preserve actual actor decisions, subject identity and known limitations.

how_much.scope: This allocated contribution to SR-081; other contributors, independent assessment, physical recording implementation and product activation remain distinct.

acceptance_criteria: Keep IR/SR and stakeholder intent, logical Functions, and Module/Interface/AR realization under their respective authoring methods.
Explain allocation and applicable 4+1 methods without introducing separate technique approvals or substituting delivery tasks for ARs.
assumptions: The selected project contract, scope and required counterpart contributions are identifiable; absence is reported rather than inferred.
constraints: This draft allocation neither activates replacement runtime contracts nor proves implementation or satisfaction.

sources.basis: Draft integrated design from the accepted requirement-first basis. This defines target responsibility and cooperation, not installed capability, design approval, runtime evidence or SQLite adoption.
